title: a-var-script-slot-runs-a-proof-only-through-its-loop
intention: proofgate judges a $var in a python script slot as a proof run only when a for-loop in the same command binds that variable to a proofs glob, so a script named through any other variable is never wrapped because some other segment, or some argument, names a proof.
why: Measured 2026-10-06, n=3: bin/cmd/proofgate _runs_a_proof judges a $var script slot by PROOF_GLOB.search(whole), the whole command text. So 'PYTHONPATH=. python3 $S/x.py; bin/cairn test <dir>/proofs/test_a.py' and 'python3 $S/x.py <dir>/proofs/test_a.py' are both rewritten into bin/cairn test --exec, though neither runs a proof by python. The same day it wrapped the 67af8b743a63 PROVEME crossing (python3 $S/cross.py ... <proof path>). Since 67af8b743a63, a cairn test --seal nested inside --exec is REFUSED (the network seal cannot be built), so the over-wrap turns a harmless detour into a loud refusal in every session. 72a37498c601 clause 6 (a proof path as an argument is not a proof run) is the rule; the $var branch still breaks it.
traces_to: CP4 (a gate that rewrites innocent commands chafes every session) and Law 9 / 72a37498c601 clause 6 (a proof path as an argument is not a proof run; the $var branch still makes it one)
how: In bin/cmd/proofgate: _verdict first walks every segment of the command and collects loop_vars, the NAMEs of segments whose tokens start ['for', NAME, 'in', ...] with any later token matching PROOF_GLOB. _runs_a_proof(args, loop_vars) replaces _runs_a_proof(args, whole): its $-branch strips the leading '$' and an optional '{...}' and is a proof run only when that name is in loop_vars. Any other $var slot is an ordinary script: not a proof run. A bash -c / eval string keeps its recursive _verdict, so a loop inside it binds in its own call. The docstring cites 66ae6f4a2c0e. The proof is NEW, at bin/proofs/test_a_var_script_slot_runs_a_proof_only_through_its_loop.py: it loads the gate by location as test_proof_gate.py's _gate() does and calls judge() directly. Tooth 1: judge('PYTHONPATH=. python3 $S/x.py; bin/cairn test cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a.py') is None. Tooth 2: judge('python3 $S/x.py cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a.py') is None. Tooth 3: judge('for p in cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_*.py; do python3 "$p"; done') and the ${p} spelling both rewrite to '<repo>/bin/cairn test --exec ' + shlex.quote(original). bin/proofs/test_proof_gate.py is not edited and stays green. Run with bin/cairn test.
falsifier: RED if after the build: (1) judge('PYTHONPATH=. python3 $S/x.py; bin/cairn test cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a.py') returns anything but None; (2) judge('python3 $S/x.py cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a.py') returns anything but None; (3) judge('for p in cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_*.py; do python3 "$p"; done') or its ${p} spelling is not rewritten to cairn test --exec of the original. WRONG INTENT if a hand-run proof is measured reaching python through a variable no for-loop in the same command binds (then the glob-anywhere rule was load-bearing). Horizon: the tester seal of the new proof.
watchme: none, because every rewrite proofgate makes is announced to the session in its permissionDecisionReason (bin/cmd/proofgate TOLD), so an over-wrap is seen in the transcript the moment it happens, and the new proof beside bin/cmd/proofgate reds on drift
